questions.question_english: 11. Which of the following pairs regarding recent Supreme Court decisions and constitutional provisions is correctly matched?

key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Article 21 — Safeguards against arbitrary arrest and right to personal liberty in governance

questions.question_english: 100. In state legislative procedures, if a disagreement arises between the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council regarding an ordinary Bill, how is the deadlock resolved?
options_english: By holding a joint sitting of both the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
The Bill is automatically referred to the State Governor for executive veto action
The Bill is referred to the State High Court for formal constitutional adjudication
The Assembly’s decision prevails after specified statutory delays
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is that the Assembly’s decision prevails after specified statutory delays. Unlike the Parliament, there is no constitutional provision for a joint sitting to resolve deadlocks between the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council in state legislatures. According to Article 197, if the Legislative Council rejects, amends, or delays an ordinary bill passed by the Assembly, the Assembly can pass it a second time. Ultimately, the decision of the Assembly prevails after specified statutory delay periods.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। विधान सभा का निर्णय निर्दिष्ट वैधानिक देरी के बाद प्रबल होता है। संसद के विपरीत, राज्य विधानसभाओं में विधान सभा और विधान परिषद के बीच गतिरोधों को हल करने के लिए संयुक्त बैठक का कोई संवैधानिक प्रावधान नहीं है। अनुच्छेद 197 के अनुसार, यदि विधान परिषद विधान सभा द्वारा पारित एक साधारण विधेयक को अस्वीकार, संशोधित या विलंबित करती है, तो विधान सभा इसे दूसरी बार पारित कर सकती है। अंततः, विधान सभा का निर्णय निर्दिष्ट वैधानिक देरी के बाद प्रबल होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The Assembly’s decision prevails after specified statutory delays

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Unlike Parliament, there is no constitutional provision for a joint sitting to resolve deadlocks between the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council in state legislatures. Under Article 197, if the Legislative Council rejects, amends, or delays an ordinary bill passed by the Assembly, the Assembly can pass it a second time. The decision of the Assembly ultimately prevails after specified statutory delay periods.
